title: Evaluation of the Feasibility of Telecare-Guided Nursing Interventions by Civil Protection Personnel
summary:
This study examines whether civil protection personnel (e.g., medical assistants or paramedics) can safely perform basic nursing procedures through tele-nursing (remote guidance from registered nurses). The background to this is the growing shortage of registered nurses in crisis situations (e.g., following disasters), which jeopardizes the care of people in need of nursing care.
The study tests the following procedures:
administering fluids using a sippy cup,
transferring patients from a wheel chair into a bed,
changing ostomy bags,
changing an infusion,
administering medication via a nasogastric tube,
intramuscular injections,
pressure ulcer prevention (pressure relief).

Objective:
The aim is to determine which procedures can be safely guided via tele-nursing and which still require on-site professionals. This will result in a catalog of indications for tele-nursing to alleviate the burden on care services during crises.
Study participants:
60 healthy adults (aged 18 and older) with first-aid training, including women of childbearing age who are not using contraception. Participation takes approximately 2 hours.
conditions: Care for individuals requiring care in care settings. The measures were developed in workshops and are now being evaluated to determine whether they can be implemented via telecare.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Medical certification minimum as a first responder (course completed within the last 2 years)
- Capable of giving consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Individuals who have not taken a first aid course (no more than 2 years since the last course)
- Individuals who have completed or are currently pursuing nursing training
